newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - MFI shares tumble after sales slowdown.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - MFI shares tumble after sales slowdown.

text.p: Household goods retailer MFI Furniture Group Plc saw its shares drop almost 20 percent on Tuesday after the firm reported a surprising slowdown in sales growth in the second half.

MFI, Britain's leading furniture manufacturer and retailer, said the sales rise of 7.3 percent in the first 16 weeks of its second half was lower than that achieved in the first half. The firm said this "reflects the fact that our market place has not yet seen a sustained uplift in demand."

The slackening in sales during MFI's key winter sale, which accounts for about 30 percent of annual turnover, came as a surprise and prompted a wave of downgrades to profit forecasts. HSBC James Capel analyst Jenny Nips said she downgraded the stock, but declined to provide details.
Other retail analysts said they believed forecasts for the 1996/97 financial year had been trimmed to between 70 and 75 million pounds ($121 million) from between 80 and 90 million.

"The sales performance was about five points below our expectations," said one analyst who declined to be identified. "It's a surprise because everyone thought the encouraging sales trends pre-Christmas would have continued," he said.

In December MFI said sales in Britain in the first half were up 13.5 percent, excluding new space. But the company admitted that it had yet to see a revival in the housing market, which traditionally drives demand for household durables.

On Tuesday MFI said sales in its UK businesses had grown by 7.8 percent in the second half to date. Sales in the main retail business were 6.5 percent ahead and like-for-like sales rose by 7.1 percent.

Shares in other firms linked to household goods also suffered. Carpetright and DFS Furniture Co Plc were hit. Carpetright lost 20.5 pence to 604, while DFS fell 15 to 564.5. Kingfisher, which has B&Q home improvement stores, lost 10.5 pence to 680.
MFI shares were down 39.5 pence at 157.5, trading down to their lowest level in a year.
